To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the development of the serotonergic nervous system is dose-dependently altered by 5-methyloxytryptamine, with the lower dose (0.1 mg/Kg) causing behavioral changes in the adult, but not neurochemical changes.
prenatal exposure to serotonin agonists has dose-related effects on the development of serotonin neuronal outgrowth, and that this effect is reflected in the development of behavior.
the development of serotonergic neurons is dependent, to some degree, on the stimulation or blockade of high-affinity 5-HT receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the serotonin system and how that development is regulated by endogenous serotonin and its agonists.
the development of the serotonin system and its role in the development of behavior.
the role of serotonin in the regulation of the development of its own terminal field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
serotonin, in the form of 5-MT, has dose-related effects on the development of serotonin terminal outgrowth, and also has dose-related effects which persist into adulthood.
serotonin, via its receptors, plays a role in both the development of serotonin terminals as well as in the imprinting of behavior.
serotonin plays a critical role in the development of the serotonergic neurons, as well as in neurochemical imprintation of the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of 5-MT are dose dependent, and that the lowest dose (0.1 mg) is the most effective in terms of producing long-term effects.
5-MT is a useful tool for the study of serotonin neurodevelopment and behavior, and may be a useful model for the study of the role of serotonin in imprinting.
serotonin neurons develop under the influence of a balance between stimulatory and inhibitory receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
serotonin plays a role in the development of its own neurons and in the development of behavior, even when the neurochemistry of the adult is not altered.
serotonin plays a critical role in the development of the brain, and that this role is dose-dependent.
serotonin may play a role in regulating neuronal development.
